# MrPopov

> Daniil Popov, founder of 1703 Group in Luxembourg. I build real-time, scalable systems on Elixir/BEAM for broadcast, embedded and more, and write about it here.

Personal blog of Daniil Popov. Posts about Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, broadcast tech, Go, engineering management and life. Every post has a plain markdown version at the same URL plus `index.md`.

## Posts

- [The BEAM Is a Friendly Host: C, Rust, Svelte and WebGPU Next to Elixir](https://mrpopov.com/posts/cyanview-studio-elixir-neighbors/index.md): How a LiveView dashboard on an ARM32 camera panel became a desktop color studio: Tauri and Burrito, a dirty C NIF that builds a 3D LUT in 0.85 ms per box, one Svelte island inside LiveView, WebGPU scopes, a C++ OpenFX host and Zig cross-compiling. Plus when to use a Port, a NIF, or nothing in the VM at all. (2026-10-01)
- [CyanCamera: Turning an iPhone Into a Broadcast Camera](https://mrpopov.com/posts/cyancamera-turning-phone-into-broadcast-camera/index.md): How CyanCamera turns an iPhone into a broadcast camera: BT.709 vs BT.2020, 8-bit vs 10-bit, 3D LUTs, Apple Log, and a Metal shader that runs two chained LUTs per frame at 10-bit. (2026-09-21)
- [Make Your Phoenix Website AI Ready in Seconds](https://mrpopov.com/posts/phoenix-ai-ready-markdown-negotiation/index.md): A tiny Phoenix Plug that returns text/markdown when an AI agent asks for it. Same URL, two representations, browsers see HTML, agents see clean markdown. Validated by isitagentready.com. (2026-04-29)
- [Broadcast Grade Color Scopes in Phoenix LiveView](https://mrpopov.com/posts/phoenix-liveview-webgl-color-scopes/index.md): How we shipped real broadcast style color scopes, waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope and histogram, as a Phoenix LiveView hook backed by WebGL. No React, no separate frontend, Elixir stayed in its lane. (2026-04-19)
- [How We Cut Phoenix Memory from 300MB to 120MB on Embedded](https://mrpopov.com/posts/elixir-beam-vm-embedded-optimisation/index.md): Practical guide to reducing BEAM VM memory from 300MB to 120MB and idle CPU from 45% to 5-10% for Phoenix apps on embedded devices. Covers allocator tuning, scheduler limits, PubSub pool sizing, and other production-tested optimisations. (2026-03-05)

(2026-02-25)

(2026-02-14)

Learn how to use the _mounts counter to prevent queued events from corrupting IoT device state. (2025-10-22)
